### Key correctness points
- Combined index space: 1..61 static, 62+ dynamic newest-first; index 0 → `InvalidIndex(0)`, past-end → `InvalidIndex(n)`.
- A literal's name is resolved before insertion, so a name taken from the entry the insertion evicts stays valid.
- Size updates are allowed only before the first field (`InvalidTableSizeUpdate` otherwise) and bounded by the decoder's limit (`TableSizeExceeded(size~, max~)`).
- Huffman decoding rejects EOS symbols, >7-bit padding, and non-all-ones padding, and accepts the empty string and every octet value.
- `set_max_size` takes effect immediately and is signalled at the next `encode` as the smallest-requested size then the final size (one update when equal); the single-field forms never insert or emit updates.

- Unquoted inline comments start only at a `;`/`#` preceded by whitespace; quoted content preserves markers verbatim.
- `Doc` uses reference maps so section re-opening and duplicate-key last-wins fall out of in-place mutation.

## How it works
`parse` splits input into `Array[Char]` lines and makes one pass: blank lines and full-line `;`/`#` comments are skipped, `[` starts a section (re-opening on repeats), everything else is an entry. The first `=`/`:` separates key from value; keys are trimmed and rejected if empty or containing a control char. Quoted values close on the same line; unquoted values handle continuation (odd trailing-backslash run = marker, decided on the raw line before escapes), inline comments (marker must be preceded by whitespace), trimming, then per-carrier escape decoding. A repeated key assigns again, giving last-wins; empty sections are materialized.

`print` emits every value in double quotes (escaping `\ " \n \r \t`), and double-wraps already-quoted section names / quotes names with surrounding whitespace so `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.

Hosts handle IPv6/IPvFuture literals with brackets kept and `%25` zone ids. Resolution follows Section 5.2 in strict mode with the verbatim Section 5.2.4 dot-segment algorithm, so `http:g` stays `http:g` and the abnormal examples pass.
